item.title: NH Education Trends in Southern NH — October 16, 2026: The Southern NH Squeeze
item.description:
Alex and Jordan open the new weekly show with the trend pressing on every southern New Hampshire district at once: falling enrollment, universal school choice, and dropping state aid arriving together — and what district leaders can do about it.
Sources — NH Fiscal Policy Institute (Oct 2026), educator workforce report: https://nhfpi.org/resource/new-hampshires-educator-workforce-faces-growing-recruitment-retirement-and-affordability-pressures/ ; Keene Sentinel / Granite State News Collaborative (Aug 2026), EFA cap: https://www.keenesentinel.com/state_news/nh-s-school-voucher-program-expands-to-12-500-students-hundreds-on-wait-list/article_99646690-eb07-4c2c-bf0a-02cfb451d404.html ; Nashua Ink Link (Oct 2026), facilities plan: https://nashua.inklink.news/nashua-school-board-sets-oct-21-presentation-nov-16-vote-on-facilities-plan/ ; Manchester Ink Link (Oct 2026), class sizes and staffing: https://manchester.inklink.news/manchester-schools-see-some-class-size-improvement-but-staffing-pressures-remain/ ; NHED (Sept 2, 2026), 2026 assessment results: https://www.education.nh.gov/news-and-media/nhed-announces-2026-student-assessment-results ; Business NH Magazine, Children's Scholarship Fund NH on EFA demand: https://www.businessnhmagazine.com/article/nhrsquos-school-choice-program-hits-enrollment-cap-and-has-300-students-on-a-waitlist ; NHED charter school funding documents (FY25–FY27): https://gc.nh.gov/lba/budget/operating_budgets/2026-2027/HF_Division_II/Division II - NHED Charter School Funding Documents - 03-10-25.pdf ; Londonderry sample ballot (per-pupil and proficiency figures): https://www.londonderrynh.gov/DocumentCenter/View/2396/Sample-School-Ballot-PDF?bidId= ; PublicSchoolReview, Manchester charter schools: https://www.publicschoolreview.com/new-hampshire/manchester/charter ; Nashua Ink Link (Oct 2026), library workers rally: https://nashua.inklink.news/nashua-public-library-employees-going-on-100-days-without-new-contract-as-supporters-rally/ . To verify the WMUR Nashua M shortfall report, search WMUR for Nashua school system facing dollar 2M shortfall after state aid drops (Oct 14, 2026). To verify CNHI's EFA demographic figures, search cnhinews for EFA double percentage low-income recipients Rindge 28.7. To verify teacher salary rankings, search World Population Review average teacher salary by state 2026. Long-view enrollment figures are October 1 census data via the nhschooldata project, sourced from the NH DOE iPlatform: search nhschooldata enrollment trends.

item.title: [NH] NH Education Trends in Southern NH — October 23, 2026: HB 1817 and the Free Seat
item.description:
Alex and Jordan devote the full hour to House Bill 1817, the 2026 law giving resident Education Freedom Account students free seats in their district classes, clubs, teams, and career and technical programs while the state sends districts no funding for those seats, and trace what that means for Manchester, Nashua, Derry, Salem, and the southern New Hampshire corridor in its first fall.
Sources: - HB 1817 as adopted by both bodies, with fiscal note (NH Department of Education: likely significant cost at local, state, or both level; impact indeterminable; about $6,000 per career and technical seat): https://gc.nh.gov/bill_status/pdf.aspx?id=32821&q=billVersion - HB 1817 legislative history and votes (House 179-156, Senate 15-8, signed June 19, 2026, Chapter 183, effective August 18, 2026): https://legiscan.com/NH/bill/HB1817/2026 - NH Department of Education, Technical Assistance Advisory on HB 1817 (issued September 25, 2026; districts asked to review enrollment and fee policies): https://www.education.nh.gov/sites/g/files/ehbemt326/files/inline-documents/2026/ta-hb1817.pdf - NH Department of Education, Technical Advisory on access to public school curricular and cocurricular programs, RSA 193:1-c (home educated students in grades 7-12 counted in average daily membership for adequacy aid): http://doe.nhdoit.acsitefactory.com/sites/g/files/ehbemt326/files/inline-documents/sonh/technical-advisory-rsa193-1-c.pdf - Reaching Higher NH, Recapping the 2026 Legislative Session (HB 1817 summary, 50 percent enrollment cap, district cost warning): https://www.reachinghighernh.org/content-item/554/2026-legislative-recap - New Hampshire School Boards Association, 2026 Legislative Summary (resident-only scope, instructional time measurement unresolved): https://nhsba.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/FINAL-2026-NHSBA-LEG-SUMMARY-8.18.2026.pdf - NEA-NH, New Education Laws guide (HB 1817 access without the state support given for home education students): https://neanh.org/advocating-change/new-from-nea-nh/090526-nea-nh-legislative-update-new-education-laws-state-primary - Childrens Scholarship Fund New Hampshire, EFA program reaches 12,500-student enrollment cap for 2026-27 (13,443 eligible, 943 waitlisted): https://nh.scholarshipfund.org/new-hampshire-education-freedom-account-program-reaches-12500-student-enrollment-cap/ - RSA 194-F:2, Education Freedom Account program and qualifying expenses, including services contracted from a district public school: https://law.justia.com/codes/new-hampshire/title-xv/chapter-194-f/section-194-f-2/ - EdChoice, New Hampshire Education Freedom Account program stats (average account value about $4,795 in 2025-26, cap escalator): https://www.edchoice.org/school-choice/programs/education-freedom-account-program/ - NH Education Department Special Education Procedural Safeguards Handbook, December 2024 (parentally placed students, equitable services, services plans): https://files.smartsites.parentsquare.com/8931/nhed_special_education_procedural_safeguards_handbook_-_updated_december_2024.pdf - NH Career and Technical Education, Parents page (28 centers statewide; a two-year CTE program costs about $8,000 more than standard tuition): https://nh-cte.org/parents/ - NH School Scoop, October 13, 2026 (Manchester class size caps of 20, 25, and 24 for labs; HB 1817 summary): https://nhschoolscoop.substack.com/p/nh-school-scoop-october-13-2026
To verify items without a stable URL: (1) New Hampshire Bulletin, October 12, 2026 reporting on the September 25 advisory and district capacity, prerequisite, and tryout limits: search newhampshirebulletin.com for HB 1817 EFA public school classes October 2026. (2) Town and county EFA take-up rates (Manchester about 9 percent; Rockingham County 10 percent rising to 15 percent): search the New Hampshire Bulletin for education freedom accounts double low-income recipients, which reports the Department of Education town-level data. (3) Timberlane Regional High School CTE budget figures (about $270,000 tuition, about $156,289 transportation, 143 to 158 students) and the Londonderry CTE consultant figures (about 149 students, $2,000 to $3,000 per student): search citizenportal.ai for Timberlane Regional High School CTE budget and for Londonderry School District CTE consultant.
